title: Division of the Khalsa into Five Contingents

blocks.text: Kapoor Singh’s plan now takes ceremonial and institutional form. The Khalsa is divided into five contingents, each marked by its own standard, so that the growing Panth can preserve discipline, identity, and coordinated action without losing its shared center at Akal Takht.

The page records leading Singhs attached to the different divisions and presents the arrangement as a remembered order of service, not an improvised list. The five contingents, each marked by its own standard, show how military organization and Panthic identity are being fused into one structure.

The narrative then begins explaining why Kapoor Singh could hold such trust. The poet turns to his village, lineage, and earlier seva, grounding his authority not in inherited grandeur but in the service through which he earned lasting honor among the Khalsa.
